history.period: Built 1946; inaugurated by Mahatma Gandhi on 25 February 1946
history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: this record duplicates seq 1103 (id gita-mandir-birla-temple-mathura), which already documents the Gita Mandir (Birla Mandir) of Mathura. Kept as a separate file per the duplicate rule. The Gita Mandir - popularly the Birla Mandir - on the Mathura-Vrindavan Road was built by industrialist Jugal Kishore Birla in memory of his parents and inaugurated by Mahatma Gandhi on 25 February 1946, on the condition that it remain open to people of all castes. Designed by architect Sris Chandra Chatterjee, it blends traditional Hindu architecture with modern elements in red sandstone and marble. It is called the Gita Mandir because of the Gita Stambh, an 18-metre victory tower/pillar inscribed with all 700 verses of the Bhagavad Gita in 18 chapters. The complex also displays Krishna's chariot with Arjuna, a Hanuman temple and Garuda. Distinct from the Birla Mandir at Hyderabad (seq 2291, id birla-mandir-hyderabad) - different city, separate record. NOTE: trawell.in dates the temple to 1988, conflicting with the 1946 consensus across other sources - verify; airport distance is reported as 60 km and 75 km by different sources - verify.

name: Gita Mandir (Birla Mandir), Mathura
town_description: Mathura is an ancient city on the banks of the Yamuna in the Braj region, revered as the birthplace of Lord Krishna and counted among Hinduism's Sapta Puri (seven holy cities). A major pilgrimage centre for millennia, it is dotted with temples, ghats and kunds, and lies about 160 km south-east of Delhi on the Delhi-Agra corridor.

travel.airport: Agra Airport, about 60-75 km (sources differ); Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi, about 160 km.
travel.railway: Mathura Junction, about 5-6.5 km from the temple.
travel.road: On the Mathura-Vrindavan Road; regular buses and taxis from Delhi and Agra; auto-rickshaws and cycle rickshaws locally.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; the Geeta Jayanti fair draws thousands of devotees.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Sources conflict; commonly 5:00/5:30 AM-12:00 PM and 2:00-9:00/8:30 PM with summer/winter variation - verify locally. Morning aarti around 7:00 AM, evening aarti around 7:00 PM (per mathuravrindavantourism.com).
